assessments.reasoning: The SPDX project’s pinned generated JSON, bytes [4,987), supplies the ID, deprecation flag, operative wording and two citations. The operative wording resolves the imprecision in the SWI-exception comparison comment.
The GitHub API record for the SPDX repository’s unsigned v3.29.0 tag names 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48 as its commit target. That commit is in the generated JSON locator.

The SHA-256-matched GCC source contains both sentences of the generated form, with different line breaks. It establishes correspondence for the specific GCC file independently of resolving either seeAlso URL.

challenge.method: Check the repository and revision in each SPDX citation and compare the generated exception text, explanatory comment and template with the GCC file.
challenge.results: SPDX cites binutils-gdb libiberty/unlink-if-ordinary.c, blob e49f2f2f67bfdb10d6b2bd579b0e01cad0fd708e with hb=HEAD, and Linux arch/powerpc/lib/crtsavres.S at v6.16-rc6. Neither citation identifies the GCC 14.2.0 tree. The SPDX comment describes the library as compiled with a GNU compiler. Both the operative text and the GCC specimen place that condition on the linked files. The template also admits “GCC” wording.

limitations: The seeAlso witnesses belong to binutils-gdb and Linux. Correspondence to the GCC specimen rests on direct textual comparison. Those alternative files were not separately acquired.
Line wrapping differs. The finding makes no formal template-match or legal-equivalence determination.
reasoning: The SPDX 3.29.0 generated record gives the ID GNU-compiler-exception, the name GNU Compiler Exception and isDeprecatedLicenseId false. Its operative text agrees with the GCC libiberty specimen on the library, the GNU-compiled input files, the effect on the resulting executable and the reservation of other grounds for coverage.
